summary: IEEE 802.1 defines Connectivity Fault Management, a set of tools for monitoring and troubleshooting Ethernet networks. It gave the IETF blocks of message opcodes and TLV types, and this document sets the rules IANA follows when handing out values from those blocks.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7319 sets up two IANA lists for numbers used by Ethernet Connectivity Fault Management. New values from the blocks assigned to the IETF require a Standards Action.

questions: who assigns ethernet cfm tlv types
subtitle: IANA registration rules for the CFM OpCode and TLV type blocks.

tldr.problem: IEEE 802.1 allocated blocks of CFM OpCodes and TLV Types to the IETF, and a procedure was needed for assigning values from them.
tldr.mechanism: IANA maintains separate registries for CFM OpCodes and CFM TLV Types. Both use Standards Action for assignments in the allocated ranges 64 through 95.
tldr.outcome: The document establishes registry procedures for the IETF-allocated CFM code point blocks.

today: RFC 7319 is a Best Current Practice. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: CFM Code Point Blocks
sections.content: Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) messages have an OpCode field and can include information structured as Type-Length-Value (TLV) items. IEEE 802.1 allocated 32 OpCode values, numbered 64 through 95, and 32 TLV Type values in the same range to the IETF. RFC 7319 specifies how IANA handles assignments from those blocks.
sections.plainLanguage: CFM messages use numbers to identify message operations and data fields. IEEE 802.1 set aside values 64 through 95 in both groups for the IETF.

sections.title: The Two IANA Registries
sections.content: IANA created the Connectivity Fault Management (CFM) OAM IETF Parameters registry with two subregistries: CFM OAM IETF OpCodes and CFM OAM IETF TLV Types. Both registries list values 64 through 95 as unassigned and specify Standards Action as the registration procedure. The RFC also notes that IEEE 802.1 had allocated values 32 through 63 to the ITU-T.
sections.plainLanguage: IANA keeps one list for OpCodes and one for TLV types. A Standards Action is needed before a value is assigned from either block.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The document concerns assignment of values from the IEEE 802.1 CFM OpCode and TLV Type blocks allocated to the IETF. It states that it is not directly concerned with security.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC sets registry procedures and says it is not directly concerned with security.
